knowledge:
- key_parameters: testx, testy, testz=Data frames containing gene IDs in the first column and numeric expression levels across sections in subsequent columns, ordered left-to-right ;; mask=A 3D binary matrix (0 or 1) representing the physical shape of the sample ;; query=A character vector of gene IDs to reconstruct in estimate3dExpressions ;; genes=A character vector of candidate gene IDs to restrict the axial peak gene search in findAxialGenes
- alternatives: Iterative proportional fitting (Fienberg, 1970) as described by Junker et al. (2014) is the primary method; no alternative computational reconstruction methods are mentioned in the package documentation.
- when_to_use: When analyzing genome-wide Tomo-seq (RNA tomography) data sectioned along three orthogonal axes (x, y, z) to reconstruct 3D spatial expression patterns or identify genes with significant expression peaks along specific axes.
- pitfalls: Input data frames must have gene IDs in the first column and numeric expression levels in subsequent columns ;; Section columns must be ordered strictly from left to right of the intercept for each axis ;; The mask dimensions must match the section counts of the Tomo-seq data ;; The documentation contains a typo in the Junker 2014 download function name (doadJunker2014 instead of downloadJunker2014).

workflows.name: reconstruct_and_visualize_3d_expression
workflows.intent: Reconstruct 3D gene expression patterns from 3-axis Tomo-seq data and a spatial mask, then visualize the results.
input: mask (3D binary matrix representing sample shape)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and input data ;; 2. Reconstruct 3D expression patterns for query genes using estimate3dExpressions ;; 3. Visualize the reconstructed 3D expression using the interactive imageViewer Shiny app
workflows.code:
library(tomoseqr)
data(testx, testy, testz)
data(mask)
tomoObj <- estimate3dExpressions(
    testx,
    testy,
    testz,
    mask = mask,
    query = c("gene1", "gene2", "gene3")
)
imageViewer(tomoObj)

workflows.name: detect_axial_peak_genes
workflows.intent: Detect genes with significant differences in expression levels between sections along a specific axis.
input: testx (Tomo-seq expression data frame for an axis)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and input data ;; 2. Identify axial peak genes across all genes or a subset of candidate genes using findAxialGenes
workflows.code:
library(tomoseqr)
data(testx, testy, testz)
axialGeneTable <- findAxialGenes(testx)
print(axialGeneTable)
axialGeneTable <- findAxialGenes(testx, genes = c("gene1", "gene3"))
print(axialGeneTable)
